summary: A humorous company memo from Whizbang Widgets Inc. announcing a streamlined business travel approval process. The new One-Click Approval™ lets a manager approve trips with a single click, provided the trip has a viable business purpose. Requests must be submitted at least two weeks in advance, corporate credit cards are restricted to responsible users, and expense reconciliation moves to a 'Drag and Drop Dough' system.
one_line: Whizbang Widgets Inc. announces a playful, simplified business travel policy with One-Click Approval™, two-week advance requests, and easier expense reconciliation.
key_facts: Whizbang Widgets Inc. has replaced its old business travel approval process, compared to the labyrinth of Minos, with a streamlined system.
The new system is called One-Click Approval™ and cuts approval steps from a 'marathon to a sprint'.
A trip needs a viable business purpose, and then a single click by the employee's manager approves it.
Managers act as the gatekeepers who decide whether a trip goes ahead.
Requests for business travel must be submitted at least two weeks in advance.
Last-minute flights are discouraged in the memo.
The Fantastic Plastic Corporate credit cards are entrusted only to those who can handle them responsibly.
Misuse of corporate cards may lead to reminders at the annual 'Budgets and You' puppet show, featuring accounting's sock puppet rendition of 'Responsibility'.
The company promises to approve requests faster than one can say 'expense report'.
Expense reconciliation now uses a new system called 'Drag and Drop Dough'.
The memo is signed by 'The Team at Whizbang', with the tagline that the 'B' in bureaucracy stands for 'bye-bye'.
The memo jokes that travelers are free to jet off to foreign lands 'or at least Cincinnati'.
